'''Andrew Melvin Gooden III''' (born September 24, 1981) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who is currently a broadcaster for [[Monumental Sports Network]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/csn-mid-atlantic-names-kara-lawson-primary-wizards-analyst|title=CSN MID-ATLANTIC NAMES KARA LAWSON PRIMARY WIZARDS ANALYST|work=NBA.com|date=September 27, 2017|access-date=September 27, 2017}}</ref> The [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] played 14 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Gooden played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]], where he was a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] in 2002. He earned [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]] honors with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] after they selected him in the first round of the [[2002 NBA draft]] with the fourth overall pick.

==High school==
As a senior at [[El Cerrito High School]], Gooden led his Gauchos to the 1999 [[California Interscholastic Federation]] Boys' Division III championship game.  [[Washington Union High School]] (led by future NBA guard [[DeShawn Stevenson]]) won the championship game over El Cerrito HS by a score of 77–71.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.socalhoops.tierranet.com/archive/prepnotes/0399/washingtonunion0320.htm |title=SoCalHoops High School News |publisher=Southern Cal Hoops |access-date=March 6, 2009}}</ref>

==College career==
Gooden joined fellow freshmen [[Nick Collison]] and [[Kirk Hinrich]] for the 1999–2000 season at [[University of Kansas|Kansas]]. Although at times, Gooden was frustrated with the way things were going his freshman year, he finally adjusted to coach [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]]' system.

In his freshman year, the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Jayhawks]] went 24–10 and lost to [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] in the round of 32 during the [[2000 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2000 NCAA basketball tournament]]. The next season, the Jayhawks went 26–7 and fell to [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] in the [[2001 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2001 NCAA basketball tournament]] [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship#Regional semifinals and finals|Sweet Sixteen]].

In 2002, he led the nation in rebounding and was named [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] National Player of the Year. The Jayhawks went 33–4, including 16–0 in [[Big 12 Conference]] play to win Kansas its first conference championship since 1998. The Jayhawks advanced to their first [[Final Four]] in the [[2002 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2002 NCAA basketball tournament]] since 1993, however, they lost to the eventual national champion [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] in the semifinal.

For being named [[NABC Player of the Year]] for 2002, Gooden's jersey (#0) was retired in 2003. The ceremony occurred at halftime of a Kansas home game with [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] in what would have been Gooden's senior year had he not foregone his senior year for the NBA.

==Professional career==

=== Memphis Grizzlies (2002–2003) ===
Gooden declared himself for the draft after his junior year. Out of [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], Gooden was selected as the 4th overall pick by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in the [[2002 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gooden Goes To Grizzlies In First Round Of 2002 NBA Draft |url=https://big12sports.com/news/2002/6/27/1517507.aspx |access-date=April 15, 2023 |website=Big 12 Conference|date=June 27, 2002 }}</ref>

=== Orlando Magic (2003–2004) ===
In March 2003, Gooden and [[Gordan Giriček]] were traded to the Orlando Magic for [[Mike Miller (basketball, born 1980)|Mike Miller]], [[Ryan Humphrey]], and two draft picks.<ref name="MagicTrade">{{cite web |url=http://a.espncdn.com/nba/columns/spears_marc/1521791.html |title=ESPN.com: NBA – Gooden acquires sunny disposition in Orlando |work=ESPN.com |access-date=June 4, 2015}}</ref>

=== Cleveland Cavaliers (2004–2008) ===
[[File:Darius Songaila NBA 6.jpg|thumb|Gooden and [[Washington Wizards]] player [[Darius Songaila]] try to get a [[jump ball]] during a 2007 game]]
On July 23, 2004, the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] acquired Gooden, [[Anderson Varejão]], and [[Steven Hunter]] for [[Tony Battie]] and two second-round draft picks from the [[Orlando Magic]] via trade.<ref name="NBAbio">{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/drew_gooden/bio.html |title=Drew Gooden Bio Page |work=NBA.com |access-date=March 6, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090307122906/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/drew_gooden/bio.html |archive-date=March 7, 2009 }}</ref> On January 20, 2005, Gooden led the Cavaliers to a win over the Bucks with a career-high 33 points, including 27 in the second half.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20230729020349/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/250130005 Cavs beat Bucks with James in street clothes]</ref>

Gooden re-signed with the Cavaliers for three more years on August 14, 2006.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2549112 |title=Gooden signs three-year, $23M deal with Cavaliers |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=September 11, 2006 |access-date=March 6, 2009}}</ref> He agreed to a three-year, $23 million contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2549112 |title=Gooden signs three-year, $23M deal with Cavaliers |last=Stein |first=Marc |date=September 11, 2006 |publisher=ESPN |access-date=March 6, 2009}}</ref>

In the [[2006–07 NBA season]], he averaged 11.1 points per game and 8.5 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/drew_gooden/index.html |title=Drew Gooden: Season Averages |work=NBA.com |access-date=March 6, 2009}}</ref>

=== Chicago Bulls (2008–2009) ===
On February 21, 2008, at the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]]'s trade deadline, Gooden was traded by the Cavs (along with [[Larry Hughes]], [[Cedric Simmons]], and [[Shannon Brown]]) to the Chicago Bulls as a part of a three-team, 11-player deal involving the [[Seattle SuperSonics]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://sports.myway.com/news/02212008/v8855.html |title=Cavaliers Acquire Ben Wallace, Wally Szczerbiak in Three-way Trade With Chicago, Seattle |publisher=Sports.myway.com |access-date=March 6, 2009}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2009)===
On February 18, 2009, at the [[2008–09 NBA season|2008–09 season]]'s trade deadline, Gooden, Simmons, [[Andrés Nocioni]] and [[Michael Ruffin]] was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] for [[Brad Miller (basketball)|Brad Miller]] and [[John Salmons]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings_press_release0209.html |title=Kings acquire four players in three-team trade |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=February 18, 2009 |access-date=February 19, 2009}}</ref>

On March 1, Gooden was bought out of his contract making him a free agent after playing just one game for the Kings.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3944959 |title=Final year of Drew Gooden's deal bought out by Sacramento Kings |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=March 2, 2009 |access-date=March 6, 2009}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2009)===
On March 5, 2009, Gooden signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for the remainder of the season.<ref name="Gooden joins Spurs">{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2009/news/03/05/spurs.gooden.ap/index.html |title=Forward Gooden joins Spurs for playoff run |work=NBA.com |date=February 27, 2009 |access-date=March 6, 2009}}</ref>

=== Dallas Mavericks (2009–2010) ===
[[File:DrewGoodenMavs.jpg|thumb|Gooden with the Mavericks in 2009]]
On July 25, 2009, Gooden posted a message on his Twitter page that said "Dallas Here I Come!!!"<ref>{{cite tweet | title=Dallas here I come!!! | date=July 25, 2009 | number=2848530071 | last=Gooden | first=Drew | user=DrewGooden }}</ref>  Dallas Mavericks owner, Mark Cuban, retweeted Gooden's tweet, adding "Welcome Drew.. !".  On July 30, Gooden officially signed with the Mavericks.<ref>{{cite news | last=Stein | first=Marc | title=Sources: Gooden to sign 1-year deal | date=July 26, 2009 | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4356529 | work=espn.com }}</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2010)===
On February 13, 2010, Gooden was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] along with [[Josh Howard]], [[James Singleton (basketball)|James Singleton]], and [[Quinton Ross]] for [[Caron Butler]], [[Brendan Haywood]], and [[DeShawn Stevenson]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/trade_100213.html|title=Wizards Acquire Howard, Gooden, Singleton, and Ross From Mavericks|work=NBA.com|date=February 13, 2010|access-date=February 17, 2010}}</ref> Four days later, he was traded again, this time to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] as part of a three-team, six-player trade that sent [[Antawn Jamison]] from Washington to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], [[Žydrūnas Ilgauskas]], a [[2010 NBA draft|2010 first-round pick]] and the rights to [[Emir Preldžič]] from the Cavaliers to Washington, [[Al Thornton]] from Los Angeles to Washington, and [[Sebastian Telfair]] from Los Angeles to Cleveland. Gooden changed his number from #90 to #0 during his tenure with the Clippers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/trade_100217.html|title=Wizards Acquire Ilgauskas, Thornton and First-Round Pick In Three-Team Deal|work=NBA.com|date=February 17, 2010|access-date=February 17, 2010}}</ref>

=== Milwaukee Bucks (2010–2013) ===
On July 1, 2010, Gooden agreed to a 5-year/$32 million contract with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], which would make the Bucks his ninth team in as many seasons in the league. On April 9, 2011, he recorded his first career triple-double in a win over the Cavaliers with 15 points, 13 rebounds, and 13 assists.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310409015 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110413081402/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310409015 |url-status= dead |archive-date= April 13, 2011 |title=Cleveland Cavaliers vs. Milwaukee Bucks - Recap - April 09, 2011 - ESPN |work=[[ESPN]] |year=2011 |access-date=April 10, 2011}}</ref>

On March 7, 2012, Gooden scored a season high 27 points during a 106–104 loss to the Chicago Bulls.<ref>[https://www2.kusports.com/weblogs/hawks_nba/2012/mar/9/wednesdaythursday-recap-drew-gooden-ligh/?templates=desktop Drew Gooden lights up Chicago for season-high 27 points]</ref> On March 14, Gooden recorded his second career triple-double in a win over the Cavaliers with 15 points, 10 rebounds, and 13 assists.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cleveland Cavaliers vs. Milwaukee Bucks - Box Score - March 14, 2012 - ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=320314015}}</ref>

On July 16, 2013, the Bucks waived Gooden using the NBA's [[amnesty clause]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-designate-gooden-teams-amnesty-player | title=Bucks Designate Gooden As Team's Amnesty Player | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=July 16, 2013 | access-date=July 16, 2013}}</ref>

=== Washington Wizards (2014–2016) ===
[[File:Drew Gooden Wizards.jpg|thumb|right|Gooden with the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2014]]
On February 26, 2014, Gooden signed a 10-day contract with the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-drew-gooden-10-day-contract Wizards Sign Drew Gooden to 10-Day Contract]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://washingtonwizardsblog.monumentalnetwork.com/2014/02/25/wizards-new-post-option-drew-gooden |title=WIZARDS NEW POST OPTION: DREW GOODEN |access-date=February 26, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140309071339/http://washingtonwizardsblog.monumentalnetwork.com/2014/02/25/wizards-new-post-option-drew-gooden |archive-date=March 9, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On March 8, 2014, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Wizards.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15421 |title=Wizards sign Drew Gooden to second 10-day contract |access-date=March 9, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140309071520/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15421 |archive-date=March 9, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On March 18, 2014, he signed with the Wizards for the rest of the season.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-gooden-remainder-season Wizards Sign Gooden for Remainder of Season]</ref>

On July 18, 2014, Gooden re-signed with the Wizards.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20140725182137/http://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-re-sign-drew-gooden-0|title=Wizards Re-Sign Drew Gooden}}</ref> In the team's season opener on October 29, 2014, against the [[Miami Heat]], Gooden was named the starting power forward in what was his first of just seven starts for the season. He subsequently scored a season-high 18 points and did not top that mark for the rest of the season.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/goodedr01/gamelog/2015/ Drew Gooden 2014-15 Game Log]</ref>

On July 13, 2015, Gooden again re-signed with the Wizards.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://wizardsmysticstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/07/13/wizards-re-sign-drew-gooden|title=WIZARDS RE-SIGN DREW GOODEN|work=MonumentalNetwork.com|date=July 13, 2015|access-date=July 13, 2015|archive-date=July 14, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150714092522/http://wizardsmysticstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/07/13/wizards-re-sign-drew-gooden|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Gooden's final NBA game was played on April 13, 2016, in a 109 – 98 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]]; he recorded one point and one steal in two minutes of playing time. On July 7, 2016, the Wizards declined their option on Gooden's contract, making him an unrestricted free agent.<ref>[http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2016/07/wizards-decline-option-on-drew-gooden.html Wizards Decline Option On Drew Gooden]</ref>

In February 2018, Drew Gooden joined [[Ice Cube]]'s [[Big3|BIG3]] basketball league as co-captain of [[3's Company]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/big3-rosters-2018-drew-gooden-captain-allen-iverson-3s-company-dermarr-johnson/|title=Drew Gooden joining Big3 N|work=cbssports.com|date=Feb 6, 2018|access-date=July 13, 2019}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Gooden's mother, Ulla, is Finnish; his father, Andrew Gooden, met her while playing pro basketball in [[Äänekoski]], Finland.<ref>Jemele Hill. "[https://www.espn.com/espn/page2/story?page=hill/071004 Riding with Drew Gooden]". ESPN. October 5, 2007. Retrieved on December 30, 2008.</ref><ref>Chris Mannix. "[https://web.archive.org/web/20060409112442/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/players/04/04/first.person0410/ First Person: Drew Gooden]" ''Sports Illustrated''. April 10, 2006. Retrieved on December 30, 2008.</ref> Gooden's parents divorced later on, and he stayed with his father in [[California]]. In August 2014, Gooden attempted to get Finnish citizenship in order to play for their national team, but he failed to do so before the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]].<ref>[http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/24671872/report-wizards-drew-gooden-wont-play-for-finland-at-fiba-world-cup Report: Wizards' Drew Gooden won't play for Finland at FIBA World Cup]</ref>

Gooden enjoys playing the piano.<ref name="NBAbio" />

At the beginning of the 2006–07 season, Gooden appeared with a patch of hair on the back of his head. He refers to this hair style as a "duck tail."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/features/garbagetime_061204.html |title=Garbage Time |work=NBA.com |access-date=March 6, 2009}}</ref> Gooden said, "It is drawing a lot of attention ... One thing I've found out is even negative publicity is good publicity. At least I had the (guts) to do it." He claims women love it: "I went from not getting compliments to now being sexy."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://origin.insidebayarea.com/sports/ci_6081929 |title=Drew defends that patch of hair on neck |publisher=InsideBayArea.com |access-date=March 6, 2009 |archive-date=September 26, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070926220517/http://origin.insidebayarea.com/sports/ci_6081929 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2012, Gooden opened a [[Wingstop]] restaurant franchise in [[Altamonte Springs, Florida]].

In 2016, Gooden returned to the [[University of Kansas]] and earned his degree in communications.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/early-lead/wp/2017/03/13/it-was-a-helluva-senior-year-drew-gooden-to-graduate-15-years-after-leaving-kansas/|title='It was a helluva senior year': Drew Gooden to graduate 15 years after leaving Kansas|first1=Scott|last1=Allen|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=March 13, 2017|access-date=March 13, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article137836103.html|title=Fifteen years after leaving KU for the NBA, Drew Gooden will graduate in May|first1=Gary|last1=Bedore|work=KansasCity.com|date=March 10, 2017|access-date=March 16, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://andscape.com/features/nba-drew-gooden-university-kansas-college-degree/|title=DREW GOODEN FULFILLS PROMISE TO EARN HIS COLLEGE DEGREE After a 14-year NBA career, the former Jayhawk will walk with the Kansas graduating class on Sunday|first1=Marc|last1=Spears|work=[[Andscape]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=May 12, 2017|access-date=May 12, 2017}}</ref>
